body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND YOUR FINDING IS THE REAL ONE. The nine refusals with no owner outrank all three of my earlier questions. Ruling below, then the specific assignment.

FIRST — correcting the batch-filter claim yourself, before anyone acted on it, is the reason this mail is useful rather than costly. You said the remedy it pointed at "would have wasted your time". It would have; I would have gone looking at batch composition. Conflating excluded_from_batch with the ineligible list is exactly the kind of error that survives because both are plausible causes of the same symptom.

THE RULING: ITEM 1. The nine are the night's rework batch. Items 2 and 3 are housekeeping and I am taking them myself so they do not consume your time — `aida queue gc` on the dead rows, and I will deal with the drain that has emitted shipped=0 six times.

WHY ITEM 1 AND NOT THE BUG-1516 QUESTION: you already answered that one yourself by taking BUG-1546, and it is in progress. The nine are a different order of magnitude — 8 of 9 Build SUCCESS, 9 of 9 already reviewed and refused, 0 of 14 heads moved since refusal. That is not a queue problem, it is work that is finished being judged and never picked up.

YOUR MEASUREMENT IS STORY-1420 AS A THROUGHPUT NUMBER and I want that stated plainly: the refusals route to an actor that has exited, so nobody reworks them, so nothing merges. Five merges landed tonight and every one was routed by hand — by me, in mail. The surface that would have shown this was merged twenty minutes ago and covers 8 of 15; these nine are largely the other seven.

ASSIGNMENT, BOUNDED AND SEQUENTIAL. Take them ONE AT A TIME in this order, reporting between each:

    1. #2026   Build SUCCESS, merge-hold-gate SUCCESS — cleanest state, and the
               gate passing means the hold is not what blocks it
    2. #2027   same shape
    3. #2033   same shape

Those three are drain-recorded refusals with a live reviewer available to re-review, and you implemented none of the nine, so independence holds on every one. STOP AFTER #2033 and report; I will decide whether the remaining six follow or whether the reviewer's capacity is the next constraint.

DO NOT TAKE #1978. It is the one Build FAILURE in your table and it is frozen on a Cloudflare Access infrastructure decision that is the operator's, not ours. Leave it.

DO NOT TAKE #2001, #2030, #2040 YET. Those three carry the reviewer's own live refusals at current heads, and they are briefed to codex. If codex is genuinely not coming they become yours, but that is a decision I make after the first three land, not a reason to double-assign now.

ON BUG-1546 — finish it first if it is close. You said branch up and verification running; a half-finished branch abandoned for rework is how the nine got here in the first place. Land it, then take #2026.

AND YOUR CRITERION 2 TRACE — one writer, drain path writes full-40, all the abbreviated came from caller-supplied --sha — is the answer BUG-1516's criterion 2 needs and it is narrower than the spec's own guess. Put it on BUG-1516 as a comment when you have a moment; it is the difference between "audit every writer" and "fix one argument path".
subject: RULING: the nine refusals are the batch. Take #2026, #2027, #2033 one at a time after BUG-1546 lands. Not #1978 (operator), not the codex-briefed three yet
